title: The relative component lift is the topological fibre product with the pulled-back structure sheaf
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $P=\pi_0(|T|)$ be its space of connected components with the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite], and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a continuous map $E\to P$ of profinite spaces, let $T\times_P E$ be the relative component lift, the affine-transition inverse limit of the finite clopen stages [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site], and let $T_E$ be the affine ind-etale $T$-scheme with underlying locally ringed space $|T|\times_P E$ and inverse-image structure sheaf from $T$ [lem-zl-affine-component-site-projection]. Then there is an isomorphism $T\times_P E\cong T_E$ of $T$-schemes, natural in $E\to P$. Consequently: the underlying space of $T\times_P E$ is the topological fibre product $|T|\times_P E$ (subspace topology of $|T|\times E$); its structure sheaf is the inverse image of $\mathcal O_T$, so every stalk map of the structure morphism $T\times_P E\to T$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{T,x}\to\mathcal O_{T\times_P E,(x,s)}$; for a map $a:E\to E'$ over $P$ the induced morphism $T\times_P E\to T\times_P E'$ has underlying map $(x,s)\mapsto(x,a(s))$; and the second projection $|T|\times_P E\to E$ induces a homeomorphism $\pi_0(|T\times_P E|)\cong E$. Empty $E$ and empty $T$ are allowed.

proof.text: The relative construction already states this same mapping property for its selected coordinate. Apply the two mapping properties to each other’s coordinates to obtain maps in both directions. The uniqueness clauses make their composites identities. For each E → E′, both composites have the same E′-coordinate by coordinate naturality in the two construction theorems; uniqueness proves naturality of the isomorphism. Thus no new finite-stage or limit comparison is necessary here: it is already supplied by the relative construction’s public mapping property.

proof.text: Compose the scheme isomorphism’s underlying homeomorphism with the affine model’s pullback homeomorphism. The slice-morphism equation gives preservation of the first coordinate, and the defining lift equation gives preservation of the second. The structure morphism factors as the comparison isomorphism followed by the model’s structure morphism, hence has isomorphic stalk maps. The two coordinate identities and naturality of the relative coordinate prove the formula (x,s) ↦ (x,a(s)).

proof.text: For any scheme morphism f with isomorphic stalk maps, let b be the actual sheaf-adjunction transpose of f.c. The inverse-image stalk isomorphism c has its prescribed unit formula on germs. The equation unit ≫ f_*b = f.c and the germ formula imply c.hom ≫ stalk(b) = f.stalkMap at each point. Cancelling c shows stalk(b) is an isomorphism; the stalk criterion for sheaf morphisms makes b an isomorphism. Apply this to each relative structure morphism.

proof.text: The comparison homeomorphism induces a homeomorphism on connected-component quotients: use its continuous map and inverse on representatives. Compose with the affine model’s stated component homeomorphism. Its value on the class of x is the model coordinate of the comparison image, hence the second coordinate of the transported pullback homeomorphism. All arguments use universally quantified points and quotient representatives, and require no nonempty space.
